question: What is a primary bone tumor?

options.A: A fracture that fails to heal properly over time
options.B: An infection caused by bacteria in the bone marrow
options.C: A growth that starts directly within the bone tissue
options.D: Spread of cancer from the breast to the skeleton

explanation: Primary bone tumors originate within the skeletal structures themselves, unlike secondary tumors that travel from other parts of the body. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why must midwives be aware of bone tumors even in maternity care?

options.A: Existing bone lesions can complicate pain and mobility during pregnancy
options.B: Midwives are the primary surgeons for musculoskeletal disorders
options.C: Bone tumors prevent the normal production of amniotic fluid
options.D: Pregnant women frequently develop primary bone cancers

explanation: Women with prior or active bone tumors require careful coordination of their physical support and pain control throughout pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following describes a characteristic of benign bone tumors?

options.A: They frequently spread to the lungs and liver
options.B: They actively destroy surrounding muscle within weeks
options.C: They grow slowly and do not spread to distant sites
options.D: They are always painful and resistant to all pain meds

explanation: Benign tumors remain localized and lack the ability to metastasize to other organs in the body. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is a well-known malignant primary bone tumor?
explanation: Osteosarcoma is a fast-growing malignant bone cancer that most commonly affects adolescents and young adults. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h2)

question: Where do secondary bone tumors typically originate?

options.A: From normal calcium deposits during pregnancy
options.B: From cartilage cells inside the knee joint
options.C: From chronic bacterial infections in the marrow
options.D: From primary cancers located in other organs

explanation: Secondary bone tumors are metastatic growths that have traveled from a primary cancer site, such as the breast or lung, to the skeletal system. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h3)

question: A middle-aged female patient with a history of breast cancer presents with new, persistent lower back pain. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A normal physiological change of aging
options.B: A secondary metastatic bone deposit in the spine
options.C: A primary benign osteoid osteoma of the vertebrae
options.D: An acute case of bacterial osteomyelitis

explanation: Given her history of breast cancer, new and persistent bone pain strongly suggests metastasis to the skeletal system. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is often the earliest and most common symptom reported by patients with a bone tumor?

options.A: Sudden complete paralysis of the limbs
options.B: Persistent, dull bone pain that worsens at night
options.C: Rapid whitening of the skin over the joint
options.D: High fever accompanied by severe chills

explanation: Bone pain that lingers and becomes more intense at night is a classic warning sign of a growing skeletal neoplasm. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why do pathological fractures occur in patients with bone tumors?

options.A: The tumor destroys normal bone matrix, making it fragile
options.B: Muscles pull too tightly because of nerve irritation
options.C: Chemotherapy causes bones to dissolve completely
options.D: High calcium levels make bones brittle and dry

explanation: Tumor growth replaces healthy, strong bone with abnormal tissue, leaving the bone vulnerable to breaking under normal stress. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which diagnostic procedure provides the final, definitive confirmation of a bone tumor type?
explanation: Only examining a sample of the tumor tissue under a microscope through a biopsy can give a definitive diagnosis. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h5)

question: What does an elevated serum alkaline phosphatase level often suggest in bone pathology?

options.B: Complete absence of red blood cells
options.C: Active bone turnover, formation, or destruction
options.D: A severe lack of dietary vitamin C

explanation: Alkaline phosphatase is an enzyme produced by bone-building cells, and its levels rise when bone is actively remodeled or damaged by a tumor. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a limb-salvage surgical procedure?

options.A: To remove the tumor while preserving the function and appearance of the limb
options.B: To cure systemic infections using high doses of antibiotics
options.C: To replace all the muscles in the body with synthetic fibers
options.D: To completely amputate the affected leg above the knee joint

explanation: Limb-salvage surgery aims to excise the cancerous bone without resorting to full amputation, utilizing grafts or prosthetics. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h6)

question: When is chemotherapy commonly administered in the treatment of malignant bone tumors?

options.A: Only after the patient has fully recovered from all surgeries
options.B: Before surgery to shrink the tumor or to target microscopic spread
options.C: As a quick pain reliever instead of standard analgesics
options.D: To replace the need for any diagnostic imaging or biopsy

explanation: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy helps shrink the primary tumor mass before surgical removal and kills stray cancer cells traveling in the body. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h6)

question: A patient recovering from surgery for a malignant femur tumor is on strict bed rest. What is a key nursing priority to prevent secondary complications?

options.A: Discontinuing all pain medications to monitor natural healing
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent swelling
options.C: Encouraging heavy weight-lifting exercises in bed
options.D: Repositioning frequently and using deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis

explanation: Immobility puts patients at high risk for pressure injuries and blood clots, making repositioning and clot prevention essential nursing duties. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why is holistic psychological support particularly important for individuals diagnosed with bone cancer?

options.A: Emotional stress directly cures the underlying tumor cells
options.B: Patients face daunting treatments, lifestyle changes, and fear of the unknown
options.C: Psychological support eliminates the side effects of chemotherapy
options.D: Mental health counseling replaces the need for surgical interventions

explanation: A cancer diagnosis brings immense emotional distress, and nurses play a vital role in addressing fears, body image concerns, and coping strategies. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h7)
